title: Back-check the trainer moment budget
brief: Reproduce the chapter trainer budget independently, then check the equivalent force using an explicitly assumed arm.
supplied: Can an independent reference calculation reproduce the trainer pitch margin and expose the implied force scale?

M_available=0.5*rho*V²*S*c*dCm; M_required=Iy*target-other; margin=M_available-M_required; initial acceleration=(M_available+other)/Iy at full command. Equivalent-force order check: F_equiv=M_available/arm.

900 kg trainer; rho=1.20 kg/m³; V=20 m/s; S=27.25 m²; c=4 m; usable dCm=0.153; Iy=5000 kg m²; other=-750 N m; target=0.12 rad/s². Nose-up moment is positive about the declared CG. For the order check only, assume a perpendicular arm of 4.0 m.
Required and available moment, nominal margin (N m), and equivalent force scale (N).
The coefficient uses aircraft reference area and chord. The assumed arm is not a validated tail geometry or aerodynamic model.
Initial single-axis pitch screen at the declared condition. Constant coefficients and inertia. No proof of successful takeoff, ground clearance, stall recovery, or safe landing.
A negative opposing moment increases the required control moment; the equivalent-force calculation is a scale check, not independent aerodynamic validation.

Check units at each step: dynamic pressure in Pa, moment in N m and equivalent force in N. A negative other moment must increase demand. Compare your results with the bench after running; accepted error is ±0.01 N m or N.
Label equivalent force with its assumed arm; distinguish exact arithmetic from rounded chapter reporting.
Compute the trainer budget, then divide available moment by each displayed assumed arm to inspect scale sensitivity.
Retain the nominal arithmetic screen; independently establish coefficient applicability, actual local flow, arm and actuator constraints.

experience.scenario: Independently reproduce the trainer moment budget, then inspect the equivalent force implied by an assumed perpendicular arm.
experience.task: Enter unrounded calculation results to two decimal places and show your substitutions. Use the on-page calculation pad or your own calculator.
experience.method: First compute dynamic pressure, then capacity. Required moment subtracts other, which is already signed. Subtract demand from capacity. Divide capacity by the assumed arm for a force scale. This rearrangement does not validate actual tail aerodynamics.
experience.investigate: Compare assumed arms 2, 4 and 5 m at fixed moment. Explain why force changes while the moment budget does not.
experience.tools: Only this app and its calculation pad are needed.
